title: kv-cache: adaptive compaction and spillover-aware eviction to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: production clusters observed periodic OOMs and degraded throughput under mixed-length workloads due to KV cache fragmentation and uncoordinated spillover. This PR implements an adaptive compaction pathway and a spillover-aware eviction policy to reduce fragmentation, favor reclaiming large contiguous segments, and make spillover decisions latency-aware. Key changes: 1) compact-on-threshold: compaction is triggered when fragmentation ratio > 0.6 and free segments below low-watermark; 2) adaptive compaction work-stealing: background compaction tasks can be throttled by load and hand off to idle worker threads to avoid impacting tail latency; 3) spillover-aware eviction: when moving pages to host memory or disk, eviction selects victims that minimize future rehydration cost (prefers cold-rank keys and contiguous blocks) and respects per-tenant spill quotas; 4) hotspot-protection: short-lived KV entries are now placed in a transient shard that is exempt from compaction for a short TTL to reduce churn; 5) observability: new metrics (kv.cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv.cache.compaction_ops, kv.cache.spillover_ops, kv.cache.rehydrate_latency_p50/p95) and tracing hooks for compaction/spill paths; 6) config knobs: compaction_ratio_threshold, compaction_max_cpu_pct, spillover_policy=(latency|cost|balanced), and tenant_spill_quota. Implementation notes: compaction uses a two-phase sweep that first finds contiguous reclaimable ranges using the meta index, then atomically coalesces pages into new slabs to minimize copying; a lightweight epoch is used to avoid blocking readers. Eviction now scores candidates by (age_weight*age + freq_weight*freq + contiguity_bonus - rehydrate_cost_estimate*cost_weight) with policy parameters exposed via runtime config and defaulting to latency-biased behavior in hosted tier. Testing: unit tests for compaction invariants and scoring, integration tests using the perf-canary harness with mixed short/long-context workloads showing 28% drop in average rehydrate latency and 18% reduction in OOM incidents on stressed nodes, long-running soak on dedicated staging for 72 hours. Rollout plan: feature gated behind kv.cache.experimental.adaptive_compaction; staged rollout on Dedicated fleets with canary on 5% of nodes then 25% and full. Backport: includes a small backport to release/2026-01 to mitigate an urgent OOM regression in certain on-prem configs. Related: ENG-1245 for design doc, SUP-4421 customer report that drove the short backport.

review_comments: Ben Chang: Can you explain how compaction interacts with the existing KV read fast-path? Concerned about added latency on tail requests.

Aisha Patel: Compaction is entirely background and uses epoch_guard to avoid blocking readers; we added a max CPU throttle (compaction_max_cpu_pct) and work-stealing to avoid impacting tail latency. See new metric kv.cache.compaction_cpu_pct.
Priya Rao: We need an integration test that simulates heavy spillover at tenant quota boundaries.
Aisha Patel: Added a perf-canary scenario that runs tenant spill quota boundary tests and added assertions to ensure quotas are respected.
Ethan Cole: Please add an emergency kill-switch config and a runtime flag for immediate rollback.
Aisha Patel: Added kv.cache.experimental.adaptive_compaction enable flag and a runtime >disable_compaction endpoint; documented rollback steps in the RFC.
Ben Chang: LGTM after addressing concurrency comments and adding more assertions around slab coalescing. Approved.
Priya Rao: Approved once we add the release note and backport.
release_notes:
- Adaptive KV cache compaction to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
- Spillover-aware eviction policy that reduces rehydrate latency
- New metrics for fragmentation/compaction/spillover
